paper_relevance.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads

paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Superposition hypothesis — how transformer networks represent more features than dimensions via superposition. Foundational for mechanistic interpretability.

paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Sparse autoencoders (SAE) for disentangling superposition in transformer representations — key tool for mechanistic interpretability at scale.

paper_relevance.title: A Survey of Mechanistic Interpretability for Transformer Language Models
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Survey covering mechanistic interpretability methods: activation patching, causal tracing, circuit analysis, attention visualization — covers all 3 expected themes.

paper_relevance.relevance_reason: IOI circuit — mechanistic analysis of 26 attention heads implementing indirect object identification in GPT-2. Seminal circuit analysis paper.

paper_relevance.title: Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens

paper_relevance.relevance_reason: ROME — uses causal tracing to locate where factual associations are stored in GPT; enables surgical knowledge editing. Foundational mechanistic analysis paper.

paper_relevance.title: Codebook Features: Sparse and Discrete Interpretability for Neural Networks
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Codebook features for sparse, discrete representation of transformer internals — alternative to SAE for addressing superposition.

paper_relevance.relevance_reason: RepE — extracts linear representations of concepts (emotion, honesty) from transformer activations. Enables top-down interpretability analysis and representation control.

paper_relevance.title: Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Probing methodology for transformer representations — linear probes on attention head outputs reveal what linguistic features are encoded. Key diagnostic tool for mechanistic analysis.

paper_relevance.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 (Extended)
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Extended IOI circuit analysis — ablation studies and attention pattern analysis for understanding compositional attention head behavior in GPT-2.

paper_relevance.title: Decomposing Language Models into Understandable Components
paper_relevance.relevance_reason: Systematic decomposition of LLM components into interpretable units — combines SAEs with circuit analysis for end-to-end mechanistic understanding.

topics.reference_answer: Mechanistic interpretability analyzes transformer internals at the level of individual components. Three main themes: (1) Attention heads: Mathematical Framework (Elhage et al. 2021) defines QK/OV circuits; induction heads enable in-context learning (Olsson et al. 2022); IOI circuit (Wang et al. 2023) reverse-engineers indirect object identification in GPT-2; ROME uses causal tracing to locate factual memories. (2) Circuit analysis: ACDC automates circuit discovery via activation patching; circuits are discovered for Greater-Than, docstring, factual recall. (3) Superposition: Toy Models (Elhage et al. 2022) shows networks pack more features than dimensions; sparse autoencoders (Gao et al. 2024) disentangle superposed features at scale. Key limitation: circuits found in small models (GPT-2) may not generalize to frontier models; scalability remains an open challenge.
